newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia refuses war crimes extraditions.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia refuses war crimes extraditions.

text.p: Yugoslavia will refuse to extradite war crimes suspects sought by the United Nations but could try them at home, Interior Minister Zoran Sokolovic said on Tuesday.

He denied that Yugoslavia was under any obligation under the Bosnian peace agreement signed by Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic to surrender indictees to the U.N. war crimes court in the Netherlands.

Yugoslavia was angered by the arrest by the U.N. in Croatia last week of the former Serb mayor of Vukovar, Slavko Dokmanovic, for alleged war crimes during the 1991 Serb revolt against Croatia's secession from former Yugoslavia.
Dokmanovic had not been informed by the U.N. that he figured on its wanted list.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright reminded Milosevic in Belgrade last month that the end of its credit blockade of Yugoslavia depended on his cooperation with the court.
The U.N. indicted three former officers of the former Yugoslav army for their role in the siege of Vukovar.
Sokolovic said the three could be investigated by Yugoslavia if the court requested but would face any criminal proceedings at home.
The United States also holds Milosevic responsible for the extradition of former Bosnian Serb President Radovan Karadzic and his army commander General Ratko Mladic for war crimes.
